title: [AUT-002] Implement a real headless agent adapter with isolated role sessions
objective: Replace manual chat copy/paste with real automated agent execution while keeping the core provider-neutral.
inScope: Choose one documented headless runtime/API adapter based on the required tool, credential and cancellation capabilities; record the choice and support matrix. A general subprocess bridge or FakeAgentProvider alone is not acceptance.

Implement the existing neutral AgentProvider boundary (versioned extensions only where necessary). Launch fresh Developer/QA/Architecture/UAT sessions with gate-compiled context, distinct durable attempt/session bindings and host-enforced role tools. Review roles cannot gain Developer write privileges or inherit private developer conversation state.

Bind structured results to project/task/run/role/invocation revision and validate all fields before existing gates consume them. Developer may produce a new commit: preserve invocation identity while final validators/reviewers bind to actual source HEAD.

Provide durable dispatch/reconciliation for uncertain launch responses, bounded retries and provider session lookup/idempotency where supported. Do not blindly launch a second agent when a previous session may still write.

Implement timeout/cancellation with actual termination acknowledgement or an explicit still-running/quarantined state. Enforce budgets and credential redaction; record public execution metadata, provider/model/config version and evidence references without hidden reasoning.
Retain manual and fake providers as supported fallback/test adapters, not the automation completion proof.
**Expected surfaces:** Concrete provider adapter, session/dispatch persistence, role execution environment integration, provider capability/conformance tests, runtime setup docs.
outOfScope: No core vendor dependency, synthetic reviewer PASS, autonomous arbitrary shell permissions, fake-only demo or GUI automation requirement.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-01: At least one real provider runs all configured required roles without copying packets/results or manually switching chats.
AC-02: Every role has fresh scoped context and enforced tool permissions; Developer cannot self-approve via labels or shared session state.
AC-03: Returned results validate through the unchanged owning gates; malformed/wrong-binding output cannot advance lifecycle.
AC-04: Restart/uncertain dispatch reconciles the original session or blocks safely, without duplicate active writers.
AC-05: Cancellation/timeout and budget enforcement are honest about external work still running.
AC-06: Manual-provider compatibility and a documented neutral conformance contract remain intact.
validationPlan:
Provider contract tests plus a bounded real-provider task in an isolated configured repository. Exercise wrong/stale result bindings, transport failure, malformed output, cancellation, token/cost limits and lost dispatch acknowledgement. Distinguish test fixtures from actual independent role-run evidence.

Use applicable repository build/test/schema/contract checks. Retain exact commands/results, package/source/config identities and an acceptance-to-evidence map. Existing or fake-provider fixtures are not independent live review or task-completion evidence. This task is normal feature work, not a new canary requirement.
npm run build; npm test; python schemas/validate_fixtures.py; python schemas/validate_repository_contracts.py; npm run test:adversarial:mutations. Add issue-specific checks before admission.
